content: 1. Simvastatin levels or effects may be increased by OATP1B1 inhibitors, raising the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin decreases simvastatin levels by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 2. Rifampin reduces siponimod levels by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with moderate CYP2C9 and moderate/strong CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended, especially in patients with CYP2C9 1/3 or 2/3 genotypes. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Rifampin decreases sirolimus levels by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely. 4. Sodium bicarbonate reduces rifampin absorption when co-administered with antacids. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before antacids. Monitor closely. 5. Rifampin reduces the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Antibiotics may reduce efficacy by disrupting colonic bacterial flora needed for drug activation. Monitor closely. 6. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases rifampin toxicity by causing fluid and electrolyte abnormalities, which may lead to seizures, arrhythmias, or renal impairment. Monitor closely. 7. Rifampin decreases sofosbuvir levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters, reducing conversion to its active metabolite GS-331007. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Rifampin reduces sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. Velpatasvir is a substrate of CYP2B6, CYP2C8, and CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Rifampin decreases solifenacin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Rifampin reduces sonidegib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 11. Rifampin decreases sorafenib levels by increasing metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Rifampin reduces sotagliflozin levels by inducing UGT1A9-mediated glucuronidation, its major metabolic pathway. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Rifampin decreases sotorasib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Sotorasib also reduces rifampin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Rifampin reduces sparsentan levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely. 15. Stiripentol increases rifampin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition but is itself reduced by rifampin through CYP3A4, CYP1A2, and CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Rifampin decreases streptomycin levels by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Rifampin reduces sufentanil levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially causing withdrawal in dependent patients. Discontinuation of CYP3A4 inducers may increase sufentanil plasma concentrations. Monitor closely. 18. Rifampin increases sulbactam levels by inhibiting OATP1-mediated clearance. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Rifampin reduces sulfamethoxazole levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitor closely. 20. Rifampin increases rifampin levels when co-administered with sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid by inhibiting OAT1/3 transporters. Monitor for adverse reactions. 21. Rifampin decreases sunitinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Rifampin reduces suvorexant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If dose adjustment is required, do not exceed 20 mg/day. Monitor closely. 23. Rifampin decreases tacrolimus levels by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Rifampin reduces tadalafil levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid combination in pulmonary hypertension patients. Monitor erectile dysfunction patients for reduced efficacy. 25. Rifampin decreases tamoxifen levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Rifampin reduces tamsulosin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Rifampin decreases tasimelteon levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 28. Rifampin reduces tazemetostat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Rifampin decreases temsirolimus levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Rifampin reduces teniposide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Rifampin increases tepotinib levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended. Monitor closely. 32. Rifampin decreases terbinafine levels by inducing CYP1A2 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Rifampin reduces tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Rifampin decreases tezacaftor levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Rifampin reduces theophylline levels by inducing CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Rifampin decreases thyroid desiccated levels by increasing metabolism. Monitor closely. 37. Rifampin reduces tiagabine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 38. Rifampin decreases tibolone levels by increasing metabolism. Monitor closely. 39. Rifampin reduces ticagrelor levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid use with potent CYP3A inducers. 40. Rifampin decreases tinidazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Rifampin reduces tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to loss of antiviral efficacy and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 42. Rifampin decreases tivozanib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Rifampin reduces tizanidine levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 44. Rifampin decreases tobramycin levels by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Rifampin reduces tofacitinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially decreasing therapeutic response. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. Rifampin decreases tolterodine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 47. Rifampin reduces tolvaptan levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Rifampin decreases toremifene levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing steady-state serum concentrations. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Rifampin reduces tovorafenib levels by inducing CYP2C8 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong or moderate CYP2C8 inducers. 50. Rifampin decreases trabectedin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Rifampin reduces tramadol levels and its active metabolite (O-desmethyltramadol) by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Rifampin decreases trandolapril levels by increasing metabolism. Monitor closely. 53. Rifampin reduces trazodone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 54. Rifampin decreases triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 55. Rifampin reduces triazolam levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 56. Rifampin decreases trimethoprim levels by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely.
